summary: Join our training course focused on Gender and Social Inclusion in Climate Adaptation. Learn strategies to foster equity and resilience in climate initiatives.
lede: Gender and Social Inclusion in Climate Adaptation helps program managers, MEAL professionals, and safeguarding specialists make resilience initiatives more equitable, measurable, and credible. You will learn to identify exclusion risks, assess vulnerability and power across intersecting identities, develop inclusive adaptation options, and plan gender-responsive delivery. Through practical mapping exercises, group work, consultations, and donor negotiation role-play, you will apply safeguarding, do-no-harm, budgeting, and monitoring approaches. The five-day training provides templates and checklists to help you build inclusive indicators, strengthen climate finance proposals, and report results credibly to donors, leaders, and communities.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for a diverse group of professionals committed to climate adaptation and resilience.
audience: Climate adaptation and resilience program managers
NGO and development project officers and team
Government staff in environment, climate, agriculture, water
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) professionals
Safeguarding, protection, and social development specialists
CSR and sustainability managers in private sector
modules: Foundations of Gender and Social Inclusion in Climate Adaptation
Gendered Impacts and Inclusion Barriers in Key Sectors
Inclusive Climate Risk Assessment and Community Engagement
Designing Inclusive Adaptation Options and Activities
Safeguarding, Do-No-Harm, and Accountability in Climate Programs
Inclusive Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning for Adaptation
Communicating Inclusion Results and Reporting to Stakeholders
Integrating GESI into Climate Finance, Proposals, and Partnerships
Leadership, Change Management, and Institutionalizing Inclusion
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of climate adaptation, project management, and basic gender concepts. Experience in program design or implementation is beneficial but not mandatory.
